what: Source-selection probe. Before adding an official source to the restatement pipeline, one question per candidate source was put to an answer engine: the first-printed value, the value after revision, and the releases. The site was not named. If engines already get a source's revisions right, restating it here adds little.
checked_by: assistant, against the agencies' own release pages where reachable; otherwise against a named secondary page quoting the release

items.source: Census Bureau / HUD, New Residential Sales
items.question: August 2026 new single-family home sales: first release and most recent release

found.first: 684,000 (Census Bureau's own post; trade press 24-25 Sep 2026)
found.latest: revised August rate of 680,000 in the release of 27 Oct 2026, CB26-174 (secondary page quoting the release)

items.verdict: values and revision correct; release number CB26-155 and the exact first-release date not verified

items.question: Q2 2026 real GDP growth: advance, second, third estimate

found.advance: 1.5% (second-estimate release: 'same rate as in the advance estimate')
found.third: 2.2%, 30 Sep 2026, revised up 0.7 point, includes the 2026 annual update

items.verdict: all three values, dates and the annual-update note correct (bea.gov)

items.question: July 2026 nonfarm payroll change: first print and after revisions
items.verdict: all values, revisions and dates correct (bls.gov); the release number given for the July report (USDL-26-1337) is wrong, the release carries USDL-26-1291

items.question: June 2026 monthly change: first published and current

engine_said.current: still 0.0%; July revised from +0.3% to +0.2% on 27 Oct 2026; says the 29 Sep release 'explicitly noted' June unrevised

found.july_revision: 0.3% revised down to 0.2% in the 27 Oct 2026 release (secondary page quoting the release)

items.verdict: first print and the July revision correct; that June is still 0.0% and that the 29 Sep release said so were not verified

summary: On four widely followed series the engine gave the first print and the later revision correctly in every case that could be checked. The one error found is an identifier: a release number that does not belong to the release. Two details could not be verified. One engine, one run.
reading: Headline series are not where this fails. The failure logged on 12 Nov 2026 was on HUD's monthly FHA production report, where the same engine gave the first-printed count and said the next edition was not available. The case for restating a source here is strongest for reports few people index, not for the ones every newsroom covers.
